newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Aug 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Aug 4.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Foreign bankers have sought an assurance from Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh that the loans they have extended to 16 ailing finance companies will be honoured. The issue is raised with Chavalit by members of the Foreign Banks' Association at Government House. (BANGKOK POST, BUSINESS DAY)

- Key coalition members have agreed to all but one of the conditions set out by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) as part of its economic rescue package, as Finance officials continue talks with the agency. Deputy Prime Minister Samak Sundaravej says the only contentious condition is that Thailand must increase value added tax (VAT) from seven to 10 percent. (THE NATION, BUSINESS DAY)

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has no other choices but to accept the draft constitution otherwise he could face political bankruptcy, political reform architect Prawase Wasi says. The social critic calls for members of Thai society to join forces to push for approval of the draft charter by sending letters or fax messages in the names of individuals or organisations to members of parliament to seek their support. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Chavalit administration's attempt to restructure the state-owned Krung Thai Bank's board of directors is placing increasing pressure on president Sirin Nimmanhaeminda. The bank president has even asked the board to consider setting up an investigation team to clear his name, in the event that Chavalit administration figures accuse him of mismanagement. (BANGKOK POST)

- The government's two largest coalition members -- the New Aspiration Party (NAP) and the Chart Pattana Party (CPP) -- are battling for control over the telecommunications business, resulting in the stalled development of several important projects. A company executive involved in a project says a growing intense conflict between the two parties is an alarming signal about the future of Premier Chavalit Yongchaiyudh's eight-month administration. (THE NATION)
